test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 04 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I rode my bike to __worked those__ morning
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e.** "work this."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence* "I rode my bike to 'worked those' morning"* is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be **"work this,".**
 
• **"work this" -** This is the correct answer. The noun "work" denotes the place of employment, and "this" correctly refers to the current morning.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *"I rode my bike to work this morning".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's the explanation:
 
 
• **"worked this" **- This option is incorrect because "worked" is a verb in the past tense. We need a noun, which is "work," to denote the place where one is employed. Also, "this" is correct as it refers to the current day.
 
• **"work these"** - This option is incorrect. The word "these" is a plural demonstrative pronoun and doesn't fit in this context. We're referring to a single, specific morning (the one today), so we should use "this."
